note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent auditor, D4, owner Q-D4 (a)). RFC 9234 Section 3.1: Customer, RS-Client and Peer "MAY propagate any route learned from a Customer, or that is locally originated" to a Provider, an RS and a Peer, and "All other routes MUST NOT be propagated." Producer OTCEgressFilter (role/otc.go) suppresses when the destination remote role is provider, peer or rs and the source role (our role toward the source) is customer, peer, rs-client or rs. TestOTCEgressFilter asserts suppression for every member of both sets: Provider-learned to Provider, Peer-learned to Peer and RS, RS-learned to Provider, RS-Client-learned to Provider, Peer and RS (the rs case the earlier verdict found propagated now asserts suppression); TestOTCEgressSuppressProviderLearnedWithoutMeta covers the config fallback with nil meta. Negatives: Customer-learned reaches a Provider and a Customer, RS-Client-learned reaches a Customer and an RS-Client, so the suppression is scoped. Each set member is pinned by at least one exact assertion, so dropping a role from either set goes red; not every source-destination pair is asserted, which the set-membership producer makes redundant.
